summary: Material provenance-ceiling bypass: cloning both ingestion and media under new IDs allows a stronger binding for the same original evidence. Tests cover single-reference aliases but explicitly accept the double-alias construction.

evidence: Inspected all eight changed files and checked every diff hunk against tree/. Changes concern L02 types, admission, snapshots, tests, documentation and associated CLI help.
Compared implementation scope with plan.md and the DEFERRED entries in tree/loop/backlog.toml; no deferred functionality is implemented.
src/eval_lab/intent_v2.py:231 identifies historical registrations only through matching ingestion or media references. Changing both references escapes the ceiling.
tests/test_intent_v2.py:297 clones the same media and ingestion under new IDs; line 305 admits the resulting independent binding.
Independently enumerated all 13 timestamp weak orderings and checked the explicit oracle's SEALED labels. Reviewed rejection tests for missing reasons and borrowed seals.

Checked schema_version=2, artifact registration, nested digest validation, immediate predecessor pins and persisted SQL reference traversal in src/eval_lab/intent_v2.py and src/eval_lab/persistence.py.

Traced PilotWorkspace.snapshot and export_snapshot against test_private_snapshot_contains_binding_closure_and_freezes_exports: binding revisions and dependencies are rooted, pinned and exported; historical exports and unrelated-binding exclusion are asserted.
Checked that repository admission supplies the planned relationship validation; the separate lint command remains explicitly outside this step.
test_no_edit_can_promote_binding[alias] changes only the ingestion identity and therefore misses the dual-reference bypass.
test_registration_and_lineage_cannot_be_reset treats cloned records as a distinct registration and begins with SEALED provenance, preventing its assertions from detecting promotion.
All five changed Python files compile. Repository tests could not be independently rerun because the available Python lacks Pydantic; gate.json reports 368 passing tests.
docs/intent-provenance.md:61-63 overstates alias protection: the implementation protects aliases retaining at least one original reference, not aliases replacing both.
Verified the explicit ordering oracle independently and matched the diff SHA-256, 752 counted changed lines, sealed plan text and all 16 locally listed protected hashes.
External library and timestamp-standard claims are listed for research rather than treated as verified.
Compared every changed path and implementation addition with the sealed plan. Snapshot CLI changes only describe the authorized snapshot behavior.
Confirmed no dependency manifests, existing tests, protected artifacts, harness code or DEFERRED implementations appear in the diff.

blocking_findings.description: The provenance ceiling can be reset by cloning both registration anchors. Persist a RECONSTRUCTED binding, copy its MediaAsset under a new ID without changing its checksum/storage reference, copy its MediaIngestion under another ID while repointing media, then create a new binding with qualifying seal/plan evidence. Both reference comparisons at line 231 are false, and the new binding ID also avoids the immutable-registration check. Existing repository link validation accepts those copies; the new test explicitly demonstrates their admission at lines 297-305. Executing the extracted admission function with field-only stand-ins accepted RECONSTRUCTED to SEALED for this construction, while the control retaining the original media reference correctly rejected it. This is a source-level reproduction, not a full repository test run.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Preserve or enforce the original registration identity across cloned ingestion/media aliases, so changing both IDs cannot manufacture a fresh provenance ceiling. Add a repository regression beginning with RECONSTRUCTED provenance, cloning both anchors without a new registration event, and attempting SEALED admission. Use genuinely independent registration evidence for the distinct-registration positive case. Make the alias-protection documentation match the enforced contract.

claims_for_research.claim: Pydantic v2 BaseModel.model_copy(update=...) does not validate supplied update values.
RFC 3161 defines evidence that a datum existed before a particular time, requires a trustworthy time source, and does not examine the timestamped imprint beyond its length.
Local seal-plan-registration timestamps alone cannot prove generation followed intent sealing; witnessing intent existence does not itself witness generation.
SQLAlchemy provides a path to PostgreSQL, while this repository's PostgreSQL isolation, triggers, migrations and load behavior remain unvalidated.
